Etsy has no separate UK catalogue/ccTLD (no etsy.co.uk) -- 'UK' is reached only via the /uk/ locale path or a ship_to=GB query param on the same etsy.com marketplace. Empirically tested via curl_cffi impersonate=chrome116 (Rule 2 step 2; direct fetch returns HTTP 403, matching c234's documented access route) on 3 category pages already catalogued in c234: (1) Mirrors -- US default and ?ship_to=GB both report the identical embedded search-state total_pages:250 (Etsy's hard pagination cap); only the displayed currency/region fields in the page JSON change (observed 'INR'/'IN' on the default US-path fetch here, vs 'GBP'/'GB' on ship_to=GB and on /uk/c/... -- i.e. Etsy's default view is itself IP-geolocated, not a fixed 'US' catalogue, and /uk/ or ship_to=GB simply re-localizes currency/display). (2) Candle Chandeliers (small, uncapped category) -- total_pages:5 identical across US default, ?ship_to=GB, and /uk/c/... paths; only currency/region metadata differ. (3) Lamp Bases -- US default fetched twice back-to-back: stable at total_pages:25 both times; /uk/c/... fetched twice back-to-back: total_pages:28 then 27 (fluctuated between its own two requests). The US-vs-UK gap (25 vs 27-28, i.e. ~2-3 pages) is the same magnitude as the noise already observed within the UK fetches alone (28->27 with no locale change at all), and matches c234's own documented finding that total_pages is not a stable figure even for repeated requests against the identical URL (its Cake Stands example: 133->131). No category showed a UK total_pages value outside this known noise band, and no evidence of a UK-specific listing set (different product IDs, different category tree, or a systematic inclusion/exclusion driven by ship-to-GB filtering) was found. Conclusion: Etsy UK is the same single global marketplace as Etsy US with a locale/currency/display filter applied via /uk/ or ship_to=GB, not a genuinely distinct per-country catalogue -- this is a duplicate of S.N. 234 and is recorded here per project convention (status ok for the duplicate-reference row regardless of the referenced source's own status) with no fresh extraction performed.
